note.subject: ir
note.why_in_news: A global alliance was formed in Bengaluru on October 2, 2026, to combat diabetic foot complications and limb preservation through international cooperation.
note.fact_box: The Global Alliance for Diabetic Foot Survival and Limb Preservation includes eight major organizations like DFSI and King’s College London. It targets the 18.6 million annual diabetic foot cases, noting a 30% mortality rate for ulcers and over 70% for major amputations.

prelims_pointers.text: DFSI: Diabetic Foot Society of India is a key member of the new global alliance.
WHO: The alliance will collaborate with the World Health Organization for advocacy and data.
The alliance aims to address 18.6 million annual diabetic foot cases globally.
Bengaluru: The city served as the host for the alliance formation on October 2, 2026.

note.mains_question: Discuss the importance of multi-lateral healthcare alliances in addressing non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and the role of international cooperation in improving surgical outcomes in developing nations.

note.subject: geography
note.why_in_news: Heavy flooding in Bihar caused by Gandak River embankment breaches and Shitalpur dam overflow, necessitating large-scale rescue operations by NDRF and IAF.
note.fact_box: On October 1, 2026, breaches in the Gandak River embankments and the Shitalpur dam caused flooding in five districts of Bihar: Saran, Gopalganj, Muzaffarpur, West Champaran, and East Champaran. Water levels exceeded the Highest Flood Level (HFL) for a duration of 24 to 36 hours.

prelims_pointers.text: Gandak River: A major river in Bihar that flows into the Ganges.
NDRF: National Disaster Response Force, a specialized force for disaster management.
Flood duration: Water remained above Highest Flood Level (HFL) for 24 to 36 hours on October 1, 2026.
Saran, Gopalganj, Muzaffarpur, West Champaran, and East Champaran: Districts in Bihar affected by the 2026 flood.

note.subject: science_tech
note.why_in_news: Tamil Nadu launched its first booth-less toll plaza at Paranur using FASTag, RFID, and ANPR technology to automate toll collection and reduce traffic congestion.
note.fact_box: The Paranur toll plaza on the Chennai-Tiruchi National Highway became the first booth-less facility in Tamil Nadu on September 30, 2026. It employs a multi-lane free flow system integrating FASTag, RFID, and Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) to eliminate vehicle stops.

prelims_pointers.text: ANPR (Automatic Number Plate Recognition) uses Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to identify vehicle plates.
The booth-less system applies a 100% penalty (twice the fee) for users without tags or sufficient balance.
A 50% discount is applicable on the penalty fee if paid within 72 hours of the e-notice.
Paranur toll plaza is located on the Chennai-Tiruchi National Highway in Tamil Nadu.

note.mains_question: Discuss how the integration of RFID and ANPR technologies in infrastructure projects can enhance logistical efficiency and reduce carbon footprints in India's transport sector.

note.subject: polity
note.why_in_news: The Kerala High Court ruled against mandatory DNA testing for correcting birth records in cases of undisputed paternity, urging legislative amendments to the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.
note.fact_box: The Kerala High Court directed the government to correct a girl's father's name where the mother's first husband was mistakenly recorded. The court specifically cited the need to amend the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, and Rule 11 of the Kerala Registration of Births and Deaths Rules, 1999.

prelims_pointers.text: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969: Central legislation governing the recording of vital statistics in India.
Kerala High Court: State judiciary overseeing the application of registration rules in Kerala.
Rule 11 of Kerala Registration of Births and Deaths Rules, 1999: Specific state rule governing the correction of birth records.

note.mains_question: Discuss the balance between the state's interest in accurate civil registration and the protection of individual privacy and dignity in correcting vital records.
